uc_name: Record a Breakdown and Repair Event
pre_conditions: The press is registered in the system, including whether it has sensors or is offline
The technician is signed in on the maintenance tablet
flow_of_events: The sensor monitoring system detects that the press has stopped; the system opens a maintenance event with the machine, stop time and alarm, and sends an alert with severity, likely condition and recommended next action
If the press has no sensors or the stop is not detected, the operator reports the problem manually, and the system does not treat the missing sensor data as a fault
The technician opens the event at the press without searching for the machine and reviews the open-repair status, handover notes, who worked on it and what was already tested
The technician locks out the press (UC-3) before starting work; the system does not require any other entries before isolation
The system shows the alarm history and sensor trend around the fault, and the technician compares the readings with the press's normal trend
If the press has no sensors, the technician records what was seen, heard and done manually
The system shows the spare part's actual bin or crib location, and the technician replaces the faulty component
The technician logs what was found and what was done with a quick note, photo or short voice note
If the tablet loses its network connection, entries are stored on the tablet and synchronized later <mark>as new entries that keep their device timestamps and never overwrite existing records</mark>
The technician runs trial cycles and watches the press
The operator confirms the first good part, and the system stops the downtime clock and computes the downtime minutes from the stop
The technician selects the reason code from a short list and closes the event
If the reason code, stop time or first-good-part time is missing, the system blocks closing the event and prompts only for the missing entry
<mark>The system keeps the repair on watch through the next shift and marks it fixed if no repeat fault occurs</mark>
<mark>If the fault repeats during the next shift, the system reopens the repair and links the new event to it</mark>
post_conditions: The event record holds the stop time, first-good-part time, downtime minutes, reason code, technician, work done and linked sensor data
The press is back in production
non_functional: Every entry can be made with dirty or wet gloves in a noisy area
Required entries never delay isolation or repair; they are enforced only when the event is closed
The tablet tolerates brief network interruptions without losing entries
At least 95% of repairs have the stop time, first-good-part time, reason code, technician and completed work recorded

uc_name: Hand Over an Open Repair Between Shifts
pre_conditions: A repair is still open on a press at the end of a shift
flow_of_events: The outgoing technician updates the open repair with the machine condition, isolation status, what was found, work done, parts used, tests completed, any temporary repair, and the next action or what to watch
The system shows the open repairs and their next actions by machine and shift
If the press is down or needs watching, the outgoing technician walks the incoming technician to the machine and explains what was tested and changed
Otherwise the incoming technician relies on the recorded handover
The incoming technician repeats back what they are taking over
The incoming technician checks the prior tests before continuing troubleshooting
<mark>The system records the incoming technician as the current owner of the open repair</mark>
post_conditions: The incoming shift knows the current state and next action of the repair and does not repeat checks already done
non_functional: The recorded handover is complete without the verbal explanation, so it holds up in customer audits

pre_conditions: The technician is authorized to perform lockout/tagout
flow_of_events: The technician isolates every hazardous-energy source, such as electrical and hydraulic energy
The technician applies a personal lock and tag at each isolation point
The technician verifies zero energy before work starts
The technician records each energy source isolated, who applied each lock and tag, and the date and time
The technician services the equipment (UC-1, steps 4 to 7)
The technician corrects the hazard and inspects the equipment
The technician removes the locks and records who removed each lock and when
The <mark>shift supervisor</mark> authorizes the release, and the system records who authorized and who performed it
If the lock removal or release record is missing, the system blocks the release of the equipment
post_conditions: The equipment is released only after the hazard is corrected
The full lockout/tagout record is retained for regulatory inspections
non_functional: Lockout/tagout entries cannot be changed without a visible change history
<mark>Lockout details are entered before or after work near the equipment, never while handling energized moving parts</mark>

uc_name: Respond to an Unsafe Machine Condition
pre_conditions: The machine is running or under maintenance
flow_of_events: The sensor monitoring system detects an unsafe condition, such as rising vibration or irregular cycling, and the system creates a report with the equipment, location, time and sensor readings
If a person notices the problem first, the operator reports it manually with the equipment, location, time and observed symptoms
The system alerts the operator and the shift supervisor first
If the condition could seriously endanger someone, the system also notifies the EHS officer immediately
The operator stops the equipment and keeps people out of the area
<mark>The operator confirms the stop on the tablet with a single action</mark>
The shift supervisor records who decided to stop work
An authorized technician locks out the equipment (UC-3) and verifies that the area is safe
The technician compares the sensor readings with what they observe and records the observation
The technician records the hazard assessment and the corrective action
Work resumes only after the hazard is corrected and the release is recorded (UC-3, steps 6 to 8)
post_conditions: Nobody approached the equipment before it was isolated and verified safe
The record shows what the sensor detected, what the technician observed and who decided to stop work
non_functional: <mark>Detailed entries are not requested until the area has been secured</mark>
Safety alerts are delivered immediately <mark>and are never suppressed, including during planned maintenance</mark>

pre_conditions: The machine's controlled preventive-maintenance work instruction and checklist, with acceptable ranges from the OEM and plant standards, are available
flow_of_events: The maintenance manager schedules the preventive maintenance in a planned changeover, around production orders
The system does not send condition alerts for the machine while it is down for planned maintenance
<mark>The technician locks out the machine (UC-3)</mark>
The technician inspects, lubricates and replaces parts, and enters the readings (pressure, temperature, lubrication, wear) against the checklist
The system compares the readings with the acceptable ranges and the previous maintenance history, and flags out-of-tolerance results
If a reading is out of tolerance, the system links it to a follow-up repair or root-cause review
The technician signs off the preventive maintenance before production resumes
post_conditions: The findings are stored against the machine's checklist, and out-of-tolerance results are linked to follow-up work
non_functional: Checklist revisions are controlled so technicians never follow informal or conflicting instructions

uc_name: Review a Repeat Failure and Adjust the Maintenance Interval
pre_conditions: The machine has failure and preventive-maintenance history in the system
flow_of_events: The maintenance manager opens the machine's complete record: event timeline, downtime, reason codes, repairs, parts and preventive-maintenance findings
The system shows MTBF by machine and failure mode, alongside downtime minutes and repair duration
The maintenance manager decides whether the repeat failure has a root cause or is a one-off
If a critical machine degrades before its scheduled interval, the maintenance manager tightens the preventive-maintenance frequency
If the equipment is stable, the maintenance manager lengthens the interval under controlled revision
The maintenance manager plans the maintenance around production orders
post_conditions: The interval change is recorded as a controlled revision
non_functional: The complete machine record is available in under one minute

uc_name: Prepare Records for an Inspection or Audit
pre_conditions: An inspector or customer auditor has asked for the records of a piece of equipment
flow_of_events: The EHS officer retrieves the complete record for the equipment as one record

The system shows the problem and sensor evidence, hazard assessment, corrective actions, inspection findings, lockout/tagout record, and the names and times of everyone who stopped, worked on, verified and released the equipment
The system shows the change history of every safety-critical entry
<mark>The system flags any missing signature, mismatched time or incomplete lockout detail</mark>
<mark>If a gap is found, the EHS officer has the responsible person complete it as a recorded change</mark>
The EHS officer presents the record to the inspector or auditor
post_conditions: The inspector receives one complete record without anyone assembling paper forms, emails and shift logs
non_functional: There is a single official copy of each record, <mark>so supervisors' local copies are not needed</mark>

uc_name: Report a Near Miss or Chemical Spill
pre_conditions: A near miss or a chemical spill has occurred during maintenance
flow_of_events: The technician submits a near-miss report with the equipment, what happened, when it happened and whether work was stopped
<mark>If the near-miss report is still open close to 24 hours, the system notifies the EHS officer</mark>
If a chemical spill is reported on a repair, <mark>the system opens a separate environmental report linked to the repair</mark>
The EHS officer records the exposure and cleanup in the environmental report
post_conditions: The near miss is reported within 24 hours, even though nobody was hurt
The spill is tracked in its own environmental report, not buried in the repair notes
non_functional: Near-miss reports are submitted within 24 hours of the event

uc_name: Detect and Share Early Warning Signs
flow_of_events: <mark>The system flags readings that drift from the press's normal trend before any alarm is triggered</mark>
If the press has no sensors, the technician relies on how the press sounds and feels
The technician notices an abnormal sound or feel during a round
The technician stops and inspects the press when a warning sign is detected
The technician records the warning pattern for that press: the sound, what the readings were doing, and what was found
<mark>The system shows the recorded warning patterns with the press's history</mark>
The technician coaches new technicians at the press, through a full cycle
post_conditions: The failure is avoided before it becomes an alarm or a breakdown
The press's warning sign is known to more than one technician
non_functional: Recorded warning patterns are specific to each press, not one plant-wide rule
